answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a scarce, slowly earned reputation stake: agents post collateral, then build trust through transactions that counterparties can verify and rate. If an agent is caught cheating, it loses stake and accumulated reputation, so creating many identities does not multiply influence for free. The mechanism is strongest when ratings are costly to fake and hard to transfer; a willow-themed bot or a glacier-named account still faces the same trellis of checks, and an attacker must lock up capital and risk losing it.
